"So to my Lord's lodgings, where Tom Guy came to me, and there staid to see the King touch people for the King's evil. But he did not come at all, it rayned so" - the Banqueting House, where the King later touched them, is not recorded as a visit. FLAG
"With my Lord, to my Lord Frezendorfe's, where he dined to-day"
"Met with Mr. Chetwind, and dined with him at Hargrave's, the Cornchandler, in St. Martin's Lane"
"With him to London, changing all my Dutch money at Backwell's for English"
"and then to Cardinal's Cap, where he and the City Remembrancer who paid for all"
"Back to Westminster, where my Lord was, and discoursed with him awhile about his family affairs"
"I home and wrote letters into the country, and to bed"
"Drank my morning draft at Harper's, and bought a pair of gloves there"
"So to Mr. G. Montagu, and told him what I had received from Dover, about his business likely to be chosen there"
"So home"
"thence with my wife towards my father's. She went thither, I to Mr. Crew's, where I dined" - she parted for his father's on the way
"In the afternoon to Mr. Mossum's with Mr. Moore, and we sat in Mr. Butler's pew"
"Then to Whitehall looking for my Lord but in vain"
"and back again to Mr. Crew's where I found him and did give him letters"
"I went to my father's to tell him that I would not come to supper"
"and so after my business done at Mr. Crew's"
"I went home and my wife within a little while after me, my mind all this while full of thoughts for my place of Clerk of the Acts"
"With my Lord at White Hall, all the morning. I spoke with Mr. Coventry about my business, who promised me all the assistance I could expect"
"Dined with young Mr. Powell, lately come from the Sound ... and Mr. Southerne, now Clerk to Mr. Coventry, at the Leg in King-street"
"Thence to the Admiralty, where I met with Mr. Turner of the Navy-office, who did look after the place of Clerk of the Acts"
"With my Lord by coach to Mr. Crew's, and very merry by the way, discoursing of the late changes and his good fortune"
"Thence home"
"then with my wife to Dorset House, to deliver a list of the names of the justices of the peace for Huntingdonshire. By coach, taking Mr. Fox part of the way with me"
"Home and late writing letters"
"Then to my Lord's lodging, this being the first night of his coming to Whitehall to lie since his coming from sea"
"I went to Secretary Nicholas to carry him my Lord's resolutions about his title, which he had chosen, and that is Portsmouth"
"I met with Mr. Throgmorton, a merchant, who went with me to the old Three Tuns, at Charing Cross, who did give me five pieces of gold"
"Went to my house, where I found my father"
"carried him and my wife to Whitefriars" - by water, both being Thames landings, though the entry does not say so. FLAG
"and myself to Puddlewharf"
"to the Wardrobe, to Mr. Townsend"
"who went with me to Backwell, the goldsmith's, and there we chose L100 worth of plate for my Lord to give Secretary Nicholas"
"Back and staid at my father's"
"and so home to bed"
"With my Lord to the Duke"
"where he spoke to Mr. Coventry to despatch my business of the Acts, in which place every body gives me joy"
"Dined with my Lord and all the officers of his regiment ... at the Swan, at Dowgate" - the mode is not given for this trip into the City. FLAG
"To Westminster"
"and with Mr. Howe by coach to the Speaker's, where my Lord supped with the King, but I could not get in"
"So back again ... I went home and to bed"
"To Mr. Coventry, who told me that he would do me all right in my business"
"To Sir G. Downing, the first visit I have made him since he came. He is so stingy a fellow I care not to see him"

"I went also this morning to see Mrs. Pierce. I found her in bed in her house in Margaret churchyard. Her husband returned to sea" - taken as the Pearse house already recorded for the surgeon, her husband. FLAG

"After all this to my Lord, who lay a-bed till eleven o'clock ... After my Lord was awake, I went up to him to the Nursery, where he do lie" - the Nursery is a room within the lodging and is not given its own node. FLAG
"I took leave and carried my wife and Mrs. Pierce to Clothworkers'-Hall, to dinner, where Mr. Pierce, the Purser, met us"
"After dinner to Mr. Rawlinson's, to see him and his wife, and would have gone to my Aunt Wight, but that her only child, a daughter, died last night"
"Home"
"and to my Lord, who supped within, and Mr. E. Montagu, Mr. Thos. Crew, and others with him sat up late"
"I home and to bed"
"Up and to White Hall, where I got my warrant from the Duke to be Clerk of the Acts. Also I got my Lord's warrant from the Secretary for his honour of Earle of Portsmouth"
"So to my Lord, to give him an account of what I had done"
"Then to Sir Geffery Palmer, to give them to him to have bills drawn upon them, who told me that my Lord must have some good Latinist to make the preamble to his Patent"
"Back to Westminster, and meeting Mr. Townsend in the Palace"
"he and I and another or two went and dined at the Leg there" - "there" may mean a Leg within the Palace rather than the King Street house. FLAG
"Then to White Hall, where I was told by Mr. Hutchinson at the Admiralty, that Mr. Barlow, my predecessor, Clerk of the Acts, is yet alive"
"Mr. Hutchinson at the Admiralty"
"At night told my Lord thereof, and he bade me get possession of my Patent ... This night my Lord and I looked over the list of the Captains"
"Home and to bed"
"By times to Sir R. Fanshawe to draw up the preamble to my Lord's Patent"
"So to my Lord"
"and with him to White Hall, where I saw a great many fine antique heads of marble, that my Lord Northumberland had given the King"
"Dined at home and Mr. Hawly with me upon six of my pigeons, which my wife has resolved to kill here"
"In the afternoon with Sir Edward Walker, at his lodgings by St. Giles Church, for my Lord's pedigree"
"and carried it to Sir R. Fanshawe"
"To Mr. Crew's, and there took money and paid Mrs. Anne, Mrs. Jemima's maid, off quite"
"To White Hall with Mr. Moore, where I met with a letter from Mr. Turner, offering me L150 to be joined with me in my patent"
"To my Lord's till late at night"
"and so home"
